references.text: Earlier in the chapter, it is mentioned that Aaron shall offer a sin offering bull for himself and make atonement for himself and his household.
Describes the sin offering with a bull for the priest who has sinned, with similar rituals for blood application and atonement.
Moses instructs Aaron to present his sin offering and make atonement for himself and the people.
Describes the sin offering bull that was slaughtered during the consecration of Aaron and his sons.
The book of Hebrews explains that the high priest must offer a sacrifice for his own sins as well as for those of the people.
Contrasts Christ with the Levitical high priests, who daily had to offer sacrifices first for their own sins and then for the people's.
Refers to the high priest entering the Most Holy Place once a year with blood for his own sins and those of the people.
At the consecration of the priests, Aaron and his sons were to lay hands on the sin offering bull before it was slaughtered.
General instruction to lay a hand on the head of the sacrificial animal and slaughter it before the Lord.
